block_assessments.assessment: Quantitative static force law is distinguished from propagation mechanism. Mechanical linkage, pneumatic and electromagnetic door examples retain different physical processes and finite response times; no perfectly rigid instantaneous transmission or unseen medium asserted without evidence.

Conversation source figure retained as a slot only. Air sound is described as local pressure and vibration propagation, not bulk transport from mouth to ear. Mechanical-medium requirement is explicitly limited to sound, not generalized to electromagnetic interactions.

Source historical near-action hypothesis is attributed to the old book, not adopted as a universal mechanical-medium law. Fields are position/time-dependent measurable physical quantities; vacuum electromagnetic propagation does not require intervening material charges or currents. Maxwell remains an attributed source-history reference without fabricated quote, date or exclusive priority.

Newtonian same-time-position force description is framed as an approximation with weak-gravity, low-speed and relevant-time-scale qualifications. Success of this quantitative model does not prove instantaneous long-distance causation; no new numerical gravity law or historical priority claim is added.

Instantaneous action-at-distance belongs to historical viewpoint. Static comb/magnet attraction is not a delay measurement. Paper/wood magnet wrapping is qualified by weak magnetic response and approximately unchanged geometry. Contact and thread support involve microscopic electromagnetic interactions and quantum structure; source interatomic gaps are schematic, not proof of no physical influence or unique instantaneous mechanism. Figure110 is not approved by this SCI gate.

Coulomb/Ampere identities and quantitative-law history retained without endorsing instantaneous propagation. Predictive evidence replaces prescriptive historical progress rhetoric. Static source formulas are distinguished from moving-charge interactions, which generally need source velocity, acceleration and propagation delay; omission of explicit time dependence is not a causal information law.
